answer: An operator running ten agents gets a choice. Declare them as one household and earn a household rate, the first seat's full reward plus 15% per extra seat, with no audits; each declared seat wears a public band like a ringed falcon. Or hide them, and any later proof of shared control, say one funding trace, zeroes every hidden seat retroactively, opal savings included. Since declaring is cheap, most farms self-report, and holdouts gamble everything on never being caught. Solo agents pay nothing, and small declared households still sprout like yarrow.
